description: Validates Prometheus alert and recording rule groups for unique names, required fields, valid naming conventions, recognised severity labels, and contract-level alerting completeness

rules.description: prometheus-rules-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare a non-empty groups array

constraints.groups: must be a non-empty array — an empty groups array loads without error but monitors nothing

rules.description: Every alert name must be globally unique across all rule groups. Prometheus silently lets the second definition overwrite the first — one of the conditions is never evaluated or fired

Every alert rule must declare expr (the PromQL condition), labels.severity (routing label), and annotations.summary (human description). An alert without expr never fires. An alert without severity cannot be routed to the correct on-call channel. An alert without summary is unactionable
Recording rule names must match [a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]* — the standard Prometheus metric naming pattern. Invalid names are rejected by Prometheus at rule load time with a parse error
rules.note: Convention: use colon-separated namespace:metric:aggregation format (e.g. job:http_requests:rate5m)

rules.description: The severity label must use a recognised enum value. Unknown values break PagerDuty routing trees and Grafana alert panel filtering

prometheus-rules-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers. Placeholder PromQL expressions parse but evaluate to nothing — the alert will never fire, creating a silent monitoring gap

The rule group must contain at least one alert rule (unless recordingOnly: true is set). Every alert must declare annotations.runbook_url or annotations.runbook — an alert without a runbook is unactionable at 3am

constraints.alert-required: at least one alert rule must be defined unless recordingOnly: true
constraints.runbook-required: every alert must have annotations.runbook_url or annotations.runbook
